config.title: Incident Response & Reliability

intro.title: Incident Response & Reliability
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simulated incident response dashboard that monitors system health and triggers alerts. You will learn the core concepts of incident response workflows, including error detection, alerting, and status communication. The main technologies involved are state management for tracking incidents and event handlers for simulating system failures and recoveries. This hands-on project will help you understand how to maintain reliability by quickly identifying and addressing issues in a production environment.
intro.usecase: Incident response and reliability engineering are critical in production systems like cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure) or SaaS applications (e.g., Slack, GitHub). Developers implement real-time monitoring dashboards that display system health metrics, error rates, and incident alerts, enabling rapid diagnosis. For example, a reliability dashboard might feature panels showing service uptime, latency graphs, and automated incident ticketing forms to log and track outages. This pattern ensures teams can quickly detect, respond to, and resolve issues, maintaining high availability and user trust in live products.

objectives: Implement a basic incident alerting mechanism using a simulated webhook endpoint.
Construct a status dashboard component that displays real-time service health metrics.
Configure a simple error boundary to capture and report frontend failures.
Integrate a logging utility to record incident details and recovery actions.
Apply a retry strategy for failed API calls to improve service reliability.
Initialize a mock incident response workflow with defined escalation steps.
Manipulate system state to simulate and recover from a degraded service condition.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react' to enable state management in the incident response component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the IncidentResponse component
steps.instruction: Define a functional component named IncidentResponse that returns a JSX fragment.
steps.hint: Create a component that will serve as the main container for the incident response interface.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define the IncidentResponse component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named IncidentResponse is defined and ready to contain the incident response UI.
successCriteria: The IncidentResponse component is defined as a function that returns a JSX fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named IncidentResponse that returns JSX content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition appears to be missing or incorrect. Please create a functional component named IncidentResponse that returns a JSX fragment.

steps.title: Initialize incident state
steps.instruction: Inside the IncidentResponse component, use useState to create an incident state object with properties: isActive (boolean), severity (string), and uptime (number). Initialize isActive to false, severity to 'low', and uptime to 99.9.
steps.hint: Call useState with an object containing the initial values for isActive, severity, and uptime. Destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an incident state variable that tracks incident status and reliability metrics.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an object containing isActive: false, severity: 'low', and uptime: 99.9. The state variable and setter are properly destructured.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your state object includes all three properties: isActive (boolean), severity (string), and uptime (number). Also verify the initial values match the requirements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The incident state wasn't properly initialized. Make sure to use useState with an object containing isActive, severity, and uptime properties with the specified initial values.

steps.title: Initialize reliability metrics state
steps.instruction: Inside your IncidentResponse component, use useState to create a state variable named 'metrics' that initializes as an object with properties: responseTime (set to 0), errorRate (set to 0), and availability (set to 100).
steps.hint: Call useState with an object containing the three properties and their initial values, then destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for system metrics
const [metrics, setMetrics] = useState({ responseTime: 0, errorRate: 0, availability: 100 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'metrics' state object ready to track reliability metrics for incident response monitoring.
successCriteria: The metrics state is initialized with an object containing responseTime: 0, errorRate: 0, and availability: 100 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a state variable named 'metrics' with all three properties (responseTime, errorRate, availability) initialized with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics state isn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState with an object containing responseTime: 0, errorRate: 0, and availability: 100.

steps.title: Define incident handler functions
steps.instruction: Inside the IncidentResponse component, create three handler functions: startIncident, resolveIncident, and updateSeverity. Each should update the incident state appropriately.
steps.hint: Define these functions after your state declarations but before the return statement. Use the setIncident function to update state.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three handler functions are defined that will modify the incident state when called.
successCriteria: The component contains startIncident, resolveIncident, and updateSeverity functions that use setIncident to update state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined some handler functions, but make sure you have all three: startIncident, resolveIncident, and updateSeverity.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler functions aren't defined correctly. Check that you've created all three functions with proper state updates.

steps.title: Define reliability update handler
steps.instruction: Inside the IncidentResponse component, define a function named updateMetrics that simulates updating reliability metrics by generating random values.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates the reliabilityMetrics state with new random values for uptime, latency, and errorRate.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an updateMetrics function that can be called to simulate real-time reliability monitoring updates.
successCriteria: An updateMetrics function is defined that sets new random values for uptime, latency, and errorRate in the reliabilityMetrics state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the updateMetrics function, but make sure it properly updates all three reliability metrics (uptime, latency, errorRate) with random values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateMetrics function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that updates the reliabilityMetrics state with new random values for uptime, latency, and errorRate.

steps.title: Create the main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside the IncidentResponse component, return a main container div with two sections: one for incident status and one for reliability metrics.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div containing two child divs or sections.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a main container div with two distinct sections for incident status and reliability metrics.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a div containing two child elements (e.g., div, section) representing the two sections.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the return statement includes a div with two child elements for the two sections.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you replaced the return statement with a div containing two sections for incident status and reliability metrics.

steps.title: Display incident status and controls
steps.instruction: Inside the incident section of your component, display the current incident status and add buttons for starting and resolving incidents with onClick handlers wired to the appropriate functions.
steps.hint: You'll need to add a heading or paragraph showing the current incident status, then create two buttons that call your incident handler functions when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The incident section should show the current incident status and provide interactive buttons to start and resolve incidents.
successCriteria: The incident section displays the current incident status and contains two buttons with onClick handlers wired to the appropriate incident handler functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the status display and two buttons with onClick handlers wired to the correct functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The incident section is missing either the status display or the control buttons with proper event handlers. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Display reliability metrics
steps.instruction: In the return statement, add a new section below the incident status section to display the current response time, error rate, and availability percentage from the metrics state.
steps.hint: Create a div with a heading and three paragraphs that show the values from the reliabilityMetrics state object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying metrics in a section

System Metrics

Response Time: {metrics.responseTime}ms

Error Rate: {metrics.errorRate}%

Availability: {metrics.availability}%
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a new section with three metrics: response time, error rate, and availability percentage.
successCriteria: A metrics section is added with three paragraphs displaying responseTime, errorRate, and availability values from state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some metrics display, but make sure to show all three values: response time, error rate, and availability percentage from the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The metrics section isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're showing all three metrics from the state in separate paragraphs.

steps.title: Add metrics refresh button
steps.instruction: Add a 'Refresh Metrics' button in the metrics section and wire its onClick to the updateMetrics handler function.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the metrics section, using the onClick prop to call the updateMetrics function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an onClick handler
<button onClick={handleRefresh}>Refresh Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Refresh Metrics' button appears in the metrics section, which when clicked will trigger the updateMetrics handler to refresh reliability data.
successCriteria: The button is placed in the metrics section and has an onClick handler that calls updateMetrics.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it's in the metrics section and its onClick is wired to updateMetrics.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected. Add a 'Refresh Metrics' button with onClick={updateMetrics} in the metrics section.
